lead.headline: Nepal warns of new flooding as border disaster toll passes 750
lead.dek: Disaster authority cites rising water upstream; 734 dead and 2,498 missing in Nepal alone
body: Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority warned Sunday of possible new flooding along the Bhotekoshi River after Chinese authorities reported increased water flow upstream, five days after a glacier collapse sent a wall of water and debris through villages on both sides of the Nepal-China border.

The combined toll passed 750 on Sunday, Euronews reported: 734 dead and 2,498 missing in Nepal, with 16 dead and 546 missing on the Chinese side. The barrier lake that had threatened a second deluge largely drained through the weekend, and rescue teams from India and China joined the search after a brief halt when it overflowed.

Large concrete and suspension bridges are gone, power lines are down, and the Prithivi Highway into Kathmandu is only partially open. Residents described repeated runs to higher ground as warnings came and went; officials said the toll is likely to rise as crews reach areas still cut off.

briefs.headline: Judge blocks deporting students over pro-Palestinian speech
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Noel Wise in San Jose ruled Friday the administration cannot deport noncitizen students solely for criticizing Israel, striking parts of the deportation provisions on First and Fifth Amendment grounds.

briefs.headline: U.S. deports relative of Afghan allies to Central African Republic
briefs.summary: A Saturday flight to Bangui carried 12 Afghans, including a man whose brothers served with U.S. forces; his lawyer said a judge had barred his removal to Afghanistan over persecution fears.

briefs.headline: Medicare's $50 GLP-1 pilot excludes the sickest patients
briefs.summary: The 18-month Bridge program covers weight-loss drugs at $50 a month, but patients whose diabetes or sleep apnea already qualifies them for Part D are routed to copays of $200 to $600 instead.

briefs.headline: Pennsylvania measles deaths set off fight over Kennedy's claims
briefs.summary: The health secretary questioned whether the state's first measles deaths in 35 years happened and accused Gov. Shapiro of gaslighting; predecessor Kathleen Sebelius called it a refusal to confront the outbreak.

briefs.headline: Russian strike on Kyiv suburb kills 37, most at a care home
briefs.summary: Saturday's drone strike in the Bucha district hit a warehouse storing drone components beside a care facility; 34 of the dead were residents. Zelenskyy ordered criminal proceedings over explosives stored next to people.

briefs.headline: Iceland votes no to resuming EU membership talks
briefs.summary: The referendum failed 52.5% to 47.5%, with Reykjavik voting yes and rural coasts strongly no; the government said it will respect the result, shelving the accession question for at least two years.

briefs.headline: Haitian gang frees 13 of more than 50 taken at Kenscoff
briefs.summary: UNICEF said six children and seven women kidnapped in the Aug. 23 attack were released Friday; about 37 remain held. The raid killed at least 47 people and displaced 2,647.

briefs.headline: Turkish and Somali forces free hijacked cargo ship, kill 14 pirates
briefs.summary: Somalia's defence ministry said Saturday the Cameroon-flagged MV Latuf, seized Aug. 17 off Puntland, was freed after a 10-day operation that destroyed four pirate boats; it gave no details on the crew.

briefs.headline: Flock cameras help end Morgantown child abduction in 85 minutes
briefs.summary: A 9-year-old taken by his uncle Saturday was recovered unharmed after the suspect's truck was hotlisted and hit at Suncrest Towne Center; Monongalia deputies arrested Sean Blaney. The system is the same one Huntington is still debating.

briefs.headline: Appeals court tosses challenges to Tucker County data center permit
briefs.summary: The Intermediate Court of Appeals ruled Wednesday it lacks jurisdiction over two appeals of Fundamental Data's air permit for the 10,000-acre Thomas-Davis project; the groups can go to the Supreme Court, and the permit stands.

briefs.headline: DEP and EPA to clear solvents from former Oceana dry cleaner
briefs.summary: The agencies announced cleanup of tetrachloroethylene, sludge and drummed waste at the former Belchers Cleaners site; the governor's office said Thursday there is no immediate danger to neighbors.

regional.item: The county commission said Thursday it has received no annexation petition from Milton, which wants three miles of U.S. 60 toward Culloden.
Nitro Elementary reported burned play equipment, shattered glass and graffiti Saturday, and may close the playground if it is not cleaned by Monday.
A $20M restoration of the Rend Trail and its five century-old trestles began this month between Minden and Thurmond, finishing in late 2027.

away.item: Mechanic Street in North Bennington closes this week while highway crews replace a culvert, per the town's road-work notice.

hotspots.item: Gauley Fest, the world's largest paddling festival, returns to Summersville Sept. 17-20, with river releases planned for the festival weekend.
Topsail Beach will mark the 25th anniversary of Sept. 11 with a walk from the fire department to Town Center and a wreath-laying, announced Aug. 21.

briefs.headline: Evacuation alert lifted as Endako wildfire creeps toward Tatin Lake
briefs.summary: The Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako rescinded its alert Thursday for the lightning-sparked fire 7 km northwest of Endako, though the BC Wildfire Service expects eastward growth and warns winds could shift it.

briefs.headline: Fraser sockeye run collapses; no commercial or sport openings
briefs.summary: DFO said Friday the return is under 2.8 million fish against a midpoint forecast of 7.74 million, too low to open commercial or recreational fisheries; wildfire, drought and thin snowpack are blamed.

briefs.headline: Ottawa sends $5M to Nepal as 32 Canadians remain missing
briefs.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand announced the humanitarian funding Friday, delivered through the Red Cross and UN agencies; none of the 121 foreign nationals rescued so far are Canadian.

briefs.headline: Cosmic acceleration survives challenge, supernova analysis finds
briefs.summary: A Southampton-led team including two Nobel laureates reports in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society that a Korean study claiming the expansion is slowing mishandled supernova ages; dark energy's push stands.

briefs.headline: Pilbara iron rocks shown to make hydrogen, and to make more on demand
briefs.summary: Edith Cowan University researchers report in the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy that magnetite in hot water generates hydrogen at depth, and that injecting solutions into banded iron formations can boost the yield.

briefs.headline: More than 100 federal science advisory panels terminated
briefs.summary: NPR reports the administration has shut panels spanning long COVID, infection control, astrophysics and the NASA Advisory Council; members say guidance on threats like Candida auris is already slower.

briefs.headline: Goodfire's Silico turns interpretability into an automated lab
briefs.summary: The platform, launched Wednesday, sends agents armed with probes and sparse autoencoders into other models; UK firm Prima Mente used it to pull a novel Alzheimer's biomarker from its epigenetics model, and $1M in access goes to academics.

briefs.headline: Cerebras stacks DRAM on the wafer in next-generation AI chip plan
briefs.summary: At last week's Hot Chips conference the company said its CS-4 doubles its predecessor's tokens at 10 times the energy efficiency; a 2027 CS-5 targets 10,000 tokens per second per user, and the CS-6 adds stacked DRAM.

art.caption: The Rend Trail's leaf-strewn deck runs between wooden rails toward the trees near Minden, where a $20M restoration began this month.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore follows with the forecast at 7:15.
kicker: The Roman Space Telescope's launch window opens at 7:26 this morning, 26 minutes after this edition.
